title: Cases: -ke, -er, -e
body:
# Cases: -ke, -er, -e

Bengali adds short endings to nouns where English uses words like *to*, *'s* and *in*. You've already met all three: **amake jete hobe**, **amar khide peyeche**, **ami barite khai**.

**-ke: to / object.** Use it for the person (or pet) something is done to or given to: **ami tomake bhalobashi** (I love you), **Ollie-ke khabar dao** (give Ollie food). Things usually don't take -ke: **ami boi porchi**, not boi-ke.

**-er / -r: possession ('s / of).** After a consonant, add **-er**: kukur → **kukurer**. After a vowel, add **-r**: bondhu → **bondhur**, Ollie → **Ollie-r**, bari → **barir**.

**-e / -te / -y: location (in, at, on).** After a consonant, add **-e**: ghor → **ghore**, dokan → **dokane**. After i or u, add **-te**: bari → **barite**. After a or o, add **-y**: Kolkata → **Kolkatay**, bichana → **bichanay**.

| | -ke (to) | -r (of) | location |
|---|---|---|---|
| ami | **amake** | **amar** | |
| tumi | **tomake** | **tomar** | |
| o | **oke** | **or** | |
| ke (who) | **kake** (whom) | **kar** (whose) | |
| Ollie | Ollie-ke | Ollie-r | |
| kukur | kukur-ke | kukurer | |
| bari | | barir | barite |
| ghor | | | ghore |
| Kolkata | | Kolkatar | Kolkatay |

## Examples

- **amake ektu jol dao**: give me a little water
- **ami tomake bhalobashi**: I love you
- **ami oke dekhlam**: I saw him/her
- **tumi kake bolle?**: who did you tell?
- **Ollie-r khabar**: Ollie's food
- **amar bondhur bari**: my friend's house
- **tomar bari kothay?**: where's your house?
- **ami Kolkatay thaki**: I live in Kolkata
- **Ollie ghore ache**: Ollie is in the room
- **Ollie bichanay ghumocche**: Ollie is sleeping on the bed

## Common mistakes

- ❌ **ami tumi bhalobashi**. When you is the object, it becomes ✅ **ami tomake bhalobashi**. The same goes for ami → **amake** and o → **oke**.
- ❌ **amer**, **tumir**. The pronouns have their own forms: ✅ **amar**, ✅ **tomar**, ✅ **or**.

cards.Notes: amake = (to) me; ektu = a little; dao = give (to a friend)
amake = (to) me; bolo = say/tell (to a friend)
o → oke when it's the object
daka = to call someone over; -ke marks who
ends in a vowel sound, so just -r
kukur ends in a consonant, so -er
Kolkata ends in a, so -y for 'in'; thaki = I live
ghor + -e = in the room; ache = is (somewhere)

cards.English: Ollie is sleeping on the bed
The cat is eating at home
cards.Notes: bari + -te = at home; khacche = is eating
